sentences.en: In the spring of 2004, journalist Mark Gleason sat in the front row of a small conference room in Switzerland for a big announcement.
sentences.zh: 2004年春天，记者马克·格里森坐在瑞士一间小型会议室的前排，等待一项重大公告。
那是一场戏剧性的铺垫。

sentences.en: There was a lot of tension.
The winning bid to host the 2010 FIFA World Cup was about to be revealed, and South Africa was among the leading contenders.
sentences.zh: 2010年国际足联世界杯的主办权即将揭晓，南非是主要竞争者之一。

sentences.en: I mean, they had all the top guns go to Zurich for that particular announcement.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们派出了所有重量级人物前往苏黎世参加那次公告发布会。

sentences.en: The former president of Klerk was there.
sentences.zh: 前总统德克勒克也去了。

sentences.en: South Africa wanted to be the first African nation to host the World Cup.
sentences.zh: 南非希望成为第一个举办世界杯的非洲国家。

sentences.en: They also wanted the tournament to be the start of a new chapter.
sentences.zh: 他们也希望这届赛事能成为新篇章的开始。

sentences.en: During apartheid, the country was banned from the international sporting community.
sentences.zh: 在种族隔离时期，该国曾被国际体育界禁赛。

sentences.en: Now they were on the precipice of hosting soccer's biggest event.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们正处于举办足球界最大盛事的边缘。

sentences.en: South Africans gathered in the streets of Johannesburg, Cape Town, and Durban to await FIFA's decision.
sentences.zh: 南非人聚集在约翰内斯堡、开普敦和德班的街头，等待国际足联的决定。
我和你们一起见证了那一刻。

sentences.en: So, the 2010 FIFA World Cup will be organized in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以，2010年国际足联世界杯将在南非举办。

sentences.en: You know, South Africa had come full circle in the sense of its horrible past and how it had moved on from being a pariah state
sentences.zh: 你知道，南非已经走出了可怕的过去，不再是一个被排斥的国家，这标志着它完成了一个完整的轮回，

sentences.en: and was now, you know, hosting the biggest event in world sport and very much part of the international family.
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道，它正在举办世界体育界最大的赛事，并真正成为了国际大家庭的一员。

sentences.en: The celebrations that erupted that day in Zurich were full of cheers and whistles,
sentences.zh: 那天在苏黎世爆发的庆祝活动充满了欢呼和哨声，

sentences.en: but also one notorious sound that came to define South Africa's World Cup.
sentences.zh: 但也伴随着一种后来定义了南非世界杯的著名声音。
那就是呜呜祖拉的声音。

sentences.en: Back in 2004, nobody really talked about Vuvuzelas.
sentences.zh: 早在2004年，几乎没人谈论呜呜祖拉。

sentences.en: Even people in the soccer world didn't know what they were.
sentences.zh: 即使是足球界的人也不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: But, six years later, by the time the first game of the tournament was underway, the Vuvuzela was the hottest word in sports.
sentences.zh: 但是，六年后的今天，当锦标赛的第一场比赛开始时，呜呜祖拉成了体育界最热门的词汇。

sentences.en: The Vuvuzela is a two-foot-long injection-molded plastic horn.
sentences.zh: 呜呜祖拉是一种两英尺长的注塑塑料喇叭。

sentences.en: It plays only one note, a B-flat, and it gradually became a regular feature of South African soccer.
sentences.zh: 它只能吹出一个音符，即降B调，并逐渐成为南非足球的常态特征。

sentences.en: But, prior to the 2010 World Cup, the rest of the world had never heard anything quite like it.
sentences.zh: 但是，在2010年世界杯之前，世界其他地方从未听过类似的声音。

sentences.en: And a lot of people hated it.
It's been likened to a giant swarm of angry hornets or a herd of distraught elephants.
sentences.zh: 它被比作一群愤怒的大黄蜂或一群焦躁不安的大象。

sentences.en: So loud in the stadium with the Vuvuzelas.
